description: Matched full-board-fabric CoreMark simulations with fast physical L1 caches, an ordered RAM store queue, and optional fast multiplication.

axi_model.awready_rule: no accepted AW/pending B and cycle % 5 == 1
axi_model.wready_rule: no accepted W/pending B and cycle % 7 == 3
axi_model.read_response: 20 cycles after AR acceptance; RVALID and data held until RREADY
axi_model.write_response: 20 cycles after both AW and W acceptance; byte-strobed RAM update when BVALID is asserted; BVALID held until BREADY

firmware.compiler_version:
clang version 23.1.1
Target: riscv32-unknown-linux-gnu
Thread model: posix
InstalledDir: /usr/bin
object_code_check: iterate: identical object instruction bytes before link relocation

source_scope.capture_note: Hashes captured after the runs while the RTL and harness used by these runs were unchanged; the working tree includes uncommitted FPGA changes, so git_head alone does not identify the simulated design.
source_scope.manifest_format: Sorted path order, each line SHA256 + two spaces + repository-relative path + newline.

caveats: These are simulations of the board RTL, not FPGA hardware measurements or a physical BRAM result. The nominal 1 MHz setting gives one simulated microsecond per CPU cycle; it does not establish achievable FPGA frequency.
The synthetic RAM models fixed response delays and deterministic independent channel stalls. It omits the MIG controller, DDR device behavior, board clock-domain crossings and implementation timing.
The same profiled firmware is used in both configurations. Its timed retired count includes four extra instrumentation-boundary instructions compared with the uninstrumented 50-iteration firmware.

The sixteen profiling counters overlap and are not an additive CPI breakdown. Sequential snapshots include small boundary overhead; use Timed CPU cycles / Timed retired instructions for the reported CPI. Cache events count lookups including repeated fetches while the pipeline is held.

All code, data and stack execute from the normal RAM address range through the actual board arbitration, translation ports, caches and store queue. The workload runs in M-mode with translation and interrupts disabled; this does not measure Linux performance.
CoreMark algorithms are pinned and unchanged, both standard 2K seed sets pass their reference CRCs, and each report exceeds ten nominal timed seconds.
